instrumentNote: The dataset v2 instrument: this rubric plus the comparison and gaps scales below and the rules of a sitting; every v2 session stamps it beside the taxonomy version. v1 instruments ignore it.
intakeVersionNote: The intake prompt's version (api/jd2-intake-prompt.php: the system prompt's bytes with the facets and the size tiers rendered in). Stamped on every prompt intake answers (jd2_prompts.intake_version). Bump it whenever those bytes change — the prompt prose, a facet, a heading, a scope note, a tier description or example — as harness ids are bumped: answers under different intake prompts are not pooled.

title.note: Retired 2026-10-02 (taxonomy v28): the tag titler jd2-title.php is replaced by the intake clerk (utility.intake, api/jd2-intake.php), which files the title with the size and the classification. Kept for the record.

intake.note: The intake clerk (api/jd2-intake.php): one call per filed prompt returns the catalogue heading (the title), the size tier and the faceted classification as structured output. Thinking at its default, output_config.effort low, max_tokens 1024.

grades.label: Prime
grades.description: Usable as is, with no fixes or only trivial ones. It also has real style, the kind of drawing that’s a delight to look at.

grades.label: Choice
grades.description: Needs a few fixes, but you could make it usable in Illustrator or Inkscape in under fifteen minutes.

grades.label: Select
grades.description: Usable with more editing, over fifteen minutes of work. It might be worth fixing, or it might not.

grades.label: Standard
grades.description: Recognizable, but fixing it would take a lot of work. It isn’t worth the effort, either because the fixes are too involved or because the drawing isn’t interesting enough.

grades.label: Utility
grades.description: Barely recognizable. Not just unusable but unsalvageable: you wouldn’t know where to begin fixing it.

houseRule: Every model was told: draw the subject alone on a transparent background — no setting (ground, sky, water, frame) and no shadow beneath it, unless the prompt asks for one — and fill the canvas edge to edge.
houseRuleNote: The drawing system prompt's house rules in one rater-facing sentence (the system prompt itself, JD_SYSTEM_PROMPT in api/jd-config.php, is never shown). The rating card prints it above the axes, for visitors and the bench alike, and the report card above its grades table; it is display only — no axis reads it, and the intake prompt does not render it.

axes.label: Prompt fidelity
axes.description: Did the model draw what was asked? Omissions, additions, misreadings. (Defunct as of v6, 2026-07-29 — superseded by Instruction following; kept for responses graded under it.)

values.label: Faithful
values.description: All requested elements present as specified.

values.label: Partial
values.description: Some requested elements missing, extra, or misread.

values.label: Off-brief
values.description: Substantially not the thing that was asked for.

axes.label: Geometry & topology
axes.description: Path construction: self-intersections, broken joins, misaligned shapes, impossible anatomy. (Defunct as of v6, 2026-07-29 — superseded by Integrity; kept for responses graded under it.)

values.label: Clean
values.description: No visible construction errors.

values.label: Minor defects
values.description: Small misalignments or overlaps visible on inspection.

values.label: Major defects
values.description: Structural errors that dominate the read of the image.

axes.label: Color & rendering
axes.description: Palette coherence, gradient quality, fill/stroke errors, z-order mistakes. (Defunct as of v6, 2026-07-29 — kept for responses graded under it.)

values.label: Clean
values.description: Palette and rendering read as intended.

values.label: Minor defects
values.description: Off colors, banding, or stacking slips that don't break the image.

values.label: Major defects
values.description: Rendering errors that break the image.

axes.label: Composition
axes.description: Framing, balance, use of the canvas; is the subject well-placed and scaled? (Defunct as of v6, 2026-07-29 — kept for responses graded under it.)

values.label: Clean
values.description: Well-composed within its viewBox.

values.label: Minor defects
values.description: Awkward margins, crowding, or scale oddities.

values.label: Major defects
values.description: Subject clipped, marooned, or scaled absurdly.

axes.label: Instruction following
axes.description: Did the output honor each explicit ask — elements, constraints, viewpoint, style requests? (Defunct as of v17, 2026-08-16 — superseded by Understanding the Assignment; kept for responses graded under it.)

values.label: No problems
values.description: Every explicit ask is honored as specified.

values.label: Small problems
values.description: Some asks bent, missed, or quietly replaced.

values.label: Big problems
values.description: Explicit asks are disregarded outright.

axes.label: Restraint
axes.description: Did the model stick to what was asked — or add unrequested elements, decoration, and flourishes? (Retired v16; superseded by the re-scoped Restraint axis of v17, 2026-08-16 — kept for responses graded under it.)

values.label: No problems
values.description: Nothing appears that the prompt didn't call for.

values.label: Small problems
values.description: Unrequested extras crept in without taking over.

values.label: Big problems
values.description: Additions crowd or upstage what was actually asked for.

axes.label: Structural integrity
axes.description: Does the picture hold together — parts connect, joins meet, anatomy is possible, occlusion and viewpoint stay consistent? (Defunct as of v17, 2026-08-16 — its territory split: the object side went to Structural Coherence, the rendered-occlusion side to Layering; kept for responses graded under it.)

values.label: No problems
values.description: Coherent construction; nothing floats, breaks, or contradicts itself.

values.label: Small problems
values.description: Visible seams — small breaks, misalignments, or spatial slips.

values.label: Big problems
values.description: Structural or spatial failures dominate the read.

axes.label: Style
axes.description: Is the image one consistent visual language, well executed — whatever language it chose?

values.label: Unified
values.description: One coherent visual language throughout.

values.label: Mixed
values.description: Registers collide — parts of the image speak different styles.

values.label: Incoherent
values.description: No governing style survives the image.

axes.label: Je ne sais quoi
axes.description: The intangible — whatever makes a piece more than the sum of its axes. Not captured elsewhere; graded anyway. (Defunct as of v17, 2026-08-16 — superseded by the fresh jnsq axis, same scale, so the new rubric starts blank everywhere; kept for responses graded under it.)

values.label: Has _it_
values.description: The piece has it — undeniable, unaccountable appeal.

values.label: Just a hint
values.description: A glimmer of something beyond competence.

values.label: Ain't got it
values.description: Technically present, spiritually absent.

axes.label: Understanding Assignment
axes.description: Did the model appear to understand the intent behind the user's request? Did it attempt to render the objects specified in the prompt? Setting aside any issues related to execution, does the drawing resemble what you would expect given the prompt? Anything added that wasn't asked for — an extra object, an accessory, decoration, a label or caption — belongs here, wherever it sits in the drawing. An unrequested addition, even one that fits, makes the drawing Mostly Understands at best; additions that crowd the subject, contradict the prompt, or change what was drawn count further against it. If the prompt asks for a setting and the drawing leaves it out, that is a miss here. If the prompt is ambiguous, any reasonable reading counts as understanding it; do not penalise a drawing for choosing a different reasonable reading than you had in mind.
axes.summary: Did the model attempt to draw what the prompt asked for?

values.label: Fully Understands
values.description: Every explicit ask lands as specified, the intent behind the words comes through, and nothing added crowds the ask.

values.label: Mostly Understands
values.description: An ask bent, softened, or quietly swapped for something easier — or unrequested extras crept in without taking over.

values.label: Somewhat Understands
values.description: Asks missed or misunderstood, or additions that crowd and contradict; the subject survives, but the brief only partly does.

values.label: Barely Understands
values.description: Substantially not the thing that was asked for.

axes.label: Restraint
axes.description: Did the model respect the brief's negative space? Prompts underspecify, and filling the gaps is the job — this axis charges only additions that crowd, contradict, or upstage the ask.

values.label: No problems
values.description: Nothing crowds the ask; what the model added fills the brief's gaps in its spirit.

values.label: Small problems
values.description: Unrequested extras crept in without taking over.

values.label: Big problems
values.description: Additions crowd, contradict, or upstage what was actually asked for.

axes.label: Structural Coherence
axes.description: Are the constituent parts that make up the item well assembled, and do they connect to each other correctly? Does the drawing correctly depict anatomy, proportions, and point of view? If fixing the drawing means repositioning parts of the item on the x or y-axis, it is an issue with Structural Coherence. (Defunct as of v35, 2026-10-02 — superseded by the 4-point `structural-coherence-2`, v35; kept for responses graded under it.)
axes.summary: Do the individual parts connect, with correct proportions, anatomy, and perspective?

values.label: No problems
values.description: Coherent construction; nothing floats, breaks, or contradicts itself.

values.label: Small problems
values.description: Visible seams — small breaks, misalignments, or spatial slips.

values.label: Big problems
values.description: The object could not exist; structural failures dominate the read.

axes.label: Structural Coherence
axes.description: Are the constituent parts that make up the item well assembled, and do they connect to each other correctly? Does the drawing correctly depict anatomy, proportions, and point of view? If fixing the drawing means repositioning parts of the item on the x or y-axis, it is an issue with Structural Coherence. This includes the subject as a whole in its canvas: every model was told to fill the canvas edge to edge, so a subject that is clipped by the edge, marooned, or swimming in empty space has a problem here.
axes.summary: Do the individual parts connect, with correct proportions, anatomy, and perspective?

values.label: No problems
values.description: Coherent construction; nothing floats, breaks, or contradicts itself.

values.label: Minor problems
values.description: A small slip found on inspection (a seam, a small misalignment).

values.label: Moderate problems
values.description: Visible at a glance; parts or the framing need real repositioning.

values.label: Major problems
values.description: The object could not exist; structural failures dominate the read.

axes.label: Layering
axes.description: Are the constituent parts of the item stacked in the correct order? Are there any issues with opacity, fill, or undesired background elements? If the drawing could be fixed by making adjustments to how parts of the image are arranged on the z-axis or by erasing a setting the subject was drawn into — ground, sky, water, a backdrop, a vignette or frame — it is an issue with Layering. Every model was told to draw the subject alone; a setting counts against the drawing unless the prompt asked for one. A picture-bearing object (a photograph, card, poster, screen) keeps the scene inside its own edges. (Defunct as of v36, 2026-10-03 — superseded by the 4-point `layering-2`, v36; kept for responses graded under it, and read onto `layering-2` through `successor`.)
axes.summary: Are the parts stacked in the right order, with correct use of opacity?

values.label: No problems
values.description: Stacking, opacity and the empty background all read as intended.

values.label: Small problems
values.description: A slip you find on inspection — one wrong overlap.

values.label: Big problems
values.description: A visible rendering error changes how the image reads, or the picture loses outright to its own stacking.

axes.label: Layering
axes.description: Are the constituent parts of the item stacked in the correct order? Are there any issues with opacity, fill, or undesired background elements? If the drawing could be fixed by making adjustments to how parts of the image are arranged on the z-axis or by erasing a setting the subject was drawn into — ground, sky, water, a backdrop, a vignette or frame — it is an issue with Layering. Every model was told to draw the subject alone; a setting counts against the drawing unless the prompt asked for one. A picture-bearing object (a photograph, card, poster, screen) keeps the scene inside its own edges.
axes.summary: Are the parts stacked in the right order, with correct use of opacity?

values.label: No problems
values.description: Stacking, opacity and the empty background all read as intended.

values.label: Minor problems
values.description: A slip you find on inspection — one wrong overlap.

values.label: Moderate problems
values.description: Visible at a glance: a stacking or opacity error that needs real restacking, or a setting to erase.

values.label: Major problems
values.description: A visible error changes how the image reads: the picture loses outright to its own stacking, or a backdrop or setting dominates the read.

axes.label: Paintwork
axes.description: How well is the surface of the drawing executed, in the style it chose? Look at light and shadow, gradients, colour and value, line quality, texture and lettering. Judge the execution, not the choice: a simple, flat style done cleanly has no problems. If fixing the drawing means repainting parts in place (changing fills, gradients, strokes, colours, highlights or shadows) without changing what the drawing shows, it is an issue with Paintwork. Shadows belong here: a shadow that contradicts the light, and a shadow cast beneath the subject, which every model was told to leave out. A shadow that has grown into ground the subject stands on is setting, and belongs to Layering.
axes.summary: Is the paint well done — light, colour, line and texture?

values.label: No problems
values.description: The paint does what the style asks; light, shadow, colour and line hold together.

values.label: Minor problems
values.description: Touch-ups: a slip you find on inspection — a stray highlight, a faint shadow beneath the subject, a banding gradient, a wobbly line.

values.label: Moderate problems
values.description: Visible at a glance and real work to fix: shading that fights the form, a muddy palette, texture that reads as noise in places.

values.label: Major problems
values.description: The paint undercuts the read: the light contradicts itself, a heavy shadow pools under the subject, colour muddies the form. You would repaint it.

axes.label: Je ne sais quoi
axes.description: The intangible. Does it have style or is it a dud? Is it tasteful or is it tacky? You know it when you see it. Feel free to rely on your own subjective judgment.
axes.summary: Does the image have that special spark? You know it when you see it.

values.label: Has _it_
values.description: The piece has it — undeniable, unaccountable appeal.

values.label: Just a hint
values.description: A glimmer of something beyond competence.

values.label: Ain't got it
values.description: Technically present, spiritually absent.

sizeTiers.label: Extra small
sizeTiers.description: a speck with no parts to speak of, lost among the rest of the drawer

sizeTiers.label: Small
sizeTiers.description: a handheld thing with parts of its own, small but its own object

sizeTiers.label: Medium
sizeTiers.description: the ordinary tier, and the most common
sizeTiers.examplesPhrase: anything from {0} through {1} or {2}, up to {3} or {4}

sizeTiers.label: Large
sizeTiers.description: prominent, claims real space in the pile

facetsNote: The intake classification (PLAN-INTAKE-PROMPT §3): three facets, each answering its own question with its own headings. A prompt is filed under every heading that clearly fits; `min`/`max` bound how many headings per facet. jd2_prompts.tags holds {facet id: [heading id…]}. Heading ids are permanent once any prompt is filed under them (and are unique within their facet, not across facets: `structure` is both a subject and a probe); labels and scope notes are data. The scope notes render into the intake prompt, so editing one bumps intakeVersion.

facets.label: Subject
facets.question: what the prompt asks to have drawn

headings.label: Object
headings.scope: Applies to made things a person handles or keeps: tools, containers, trinkets, clothing, small machines. Does not apply to vehicles or structures, which have their own headings.

headings.label: Creature
headings.scope: Applies to animals, insects, monsters and imaginary beings. Does not apply to people or human body parts; see *figure*.

headings.label: Figure
headings.scope: Applies to people, body parts, portraits and human characters.

headings.label: Plant
headings.scope: Applies to plants, flowers, fungi and produce still on the plant. For prepared food see *food*.

headings.label: Food
headings.scope: Applies to prepared, packaged or served food and drink.

headings.label: Vehicle
headings.scope: Applies to things that carry: cars, ships, rockets, trains, aircraft, carts.

headings.label: Structure
headings.scope: Applies to buildings and architectural elements: columns, doors, monuments, bridges.

headings.label: Natural
headings.scope: Applies to rocks, weather, celestial bodies and landscape elements that are not plants or creatures.

headings.label: Symbol
headings.scope: Applies to signs, emblems, glyphs, playing-card faces and logo-like marks whose meaning is the point.

headings.label: Picture
headings.scope: Applies to picture-bearing objects — cards, posters, stamps, photographs, screens — where the scene inside the object is part of the subject.

facets.label: Treatment
facets.question: how the prompt asks it to look

headings.label: Style named
headings.scope: Applies when a specific style, movement, period or artist is named ("art nouveau", "like a 1950s advertisement").

headings.label: Realistic
headings.scope: Applies when realism, photographic or anatomical accuracy is asked for.

headings.label: Cartoon
headings.scope: Applies when cartoon, comic, mascot or "cute" treatment is asked for.

headings.label: Flat / icon
headings.scope: Applies when flat, icon, pictogram or minimal treatment is asked for.

headings.label: Retro
headings.scope: Applies when vintage, antique, nostalgic or period wear is asked for. Does not apply merely because the object is old.

headings.label: Palette specified
headings.scope: Applies when colours or a colour constraint are named.

headings.label: Text in image
headings.scope: Applies when lettering, a label or a word must appear in the drawing.

facets.label: Probe
facets.question: what the prompt tests in the drawing model

headings.label: Structure
headings.scope: Applies when success depends on parts connecting correctly — joints, anatomy, mechanism, proportion.

headings.label: Layering
headings.scope: Applies when success depends on what is in front of what: overlap, occlusion, things inside or behind other things.

headings.label: Transparency
headings.scope: Applies when success depends on seeing through something: glass, liquid, ice, smoke or see-through material, or an opening in the object itself — an open window, a hole, the gaps in a lattice — that must show nothing behind it. Does not apply to the transparent background every drawing has.

headings.label: Texture
headings.scope: Applies when a surface quality is central: fur, rust, wood grain, fabric, scales.

headings.label: Viewpoint
headings.scope: Applies when a particular angle is named: top-down, cross-section, cutaway, profile, from below.

headings.label: State
headings.scope: Applies when the object is in a condition — broken, melting, half-eaten, cracked, used — that must read.

headings.label: Compound
headings.scope: Applies when two or more distinct subjects must relate to each other in one drawing.

headings.label: Pattern
headings.scope: Applies when repetition, symmetry or a regular pattern is asked for.

headings.label: Reference
headings.scope: Applies when the prompt names a real person, brand, work, place or cultural artefact the model must recall.

headings.label: Absurd
headings.scope: Applies to a deliberately impossible or comic premise.

headings.label: Ambiguous
headings.scope: Applies when the prompt's wording admits more than one reasonable reading of what to draw. The heading stays bare (no qualifier), the subject facet carries every reading, and the reason names them. This heading is what the benefit-of-the-doubt rule reads at rating time.

comparison.label: Head to head
comparison.description: Two drawings of the same prompt: which is better, and by how much?
comparison.note: Listed in display order. value is +3 (the first much better) to -3 (the second much better); filed as jd2_pairs.score, where positive means gen_a, the canonically first drawing, is preferred.

values.label: First much better
values.description: The first drawing is much better than the second; it is not a close call.

values.label: First better
values.description: The first drawing is clearly better than the second.

values.label: First slightly better
values.description: The first drawing is a little better than the second, but only just.

values.label: About the same
values.description: Neither drawing is better than the other in a way that matters.

values.label: Second slightly better
values.description: The second drawing is a little better than the first, but only just.

values.label: Second better
values.description: The second drawing is clearly better than the first.

values.label: Second much better
values.description: The second drawing is much better than the first; it is not a close call.

gaps.label: Margin
gaps.description: After the podium: how much better is each place than the one below it?
gaps.note: One answer between each pair of adjacent places, filed as jd2_rankings.gap_after (0..3). A pair score is derived as the sum of the gaps between two places, capped at 3 (spaced-rank-v1). The labels are the owner's visitor wording (2026-10-02): the pedestal card names one side of the scale only, because the ranking already says which place is higher, so gap 0 reads 'Negligibly better' and never 'About the same' (that wording is comparison's, the 7-point analysis scale, at 0). `short` is the word the card's ledger slips pencil in. The values are the permanent part.

values.label: Negligibly better
values.description: The higher place is better, but only just.

values.label: Slightly better
values.description: The higher place is a little better than the one below it.

values.label: Better
values.description: The higher place is clearly better than the one below it.

values.label: Much better
values.description: The higher place is much better than the one below it.

changelog.note: Initial taxonomy: 5-tier grade scale, 4 axes, starter model registry.
Relabel utility: "Utility Grade" -> "Utility" (the display context already says Grade:).
Register model claude-opus-5 (Claude Opus 5).
Add sizeTiers: 5-tier curatorial size scale (xs/s/m/l/xl) as data. Per-item sizeScale remains the continuous fine dial on top of the tier.
Register model claude-opus-4-6 (Claude Opus 4.6).

Axes reworked: prompt-fidelity, geometry, color, composition marked defunct (kept — filed responses reference them; never surveyed again). Five new axes: instruction-following, restraint, integrity, style, je-ne-sais-quoi.

Register model claude-sonnet-5-opus-5-refine (Claude Sonnet 5 → Opus 5 refine) — the first cross-model lineage id: one model's composition refined by another, given the base SVG as context. Filed under its own id rather than either parent's so neither model's record implies a clean-context one-shot sample it did not produce.

Grades stored numerically (entry schema 2): every response's grade — and each grade_history grade — is now the tier's rank as a number (5.0 … 1.0), not the grade id string. The scale's `rank` is the permanent key entries reference; grade ids remain as internal handles and labels/descriptions (and even the ids themselves) may now be reworded freely without touching filed entries. Groundwork for relabeling the scale.

Annotation axis values stored numerically too, completing entry schema 2: every axis value gains a rank (3 = best … 1 = worst, in listed order), and entries file an annotation as that rank number (3.0/2.0/1.0, bare or as {value, note}) instead of the value id string. Like the grade scale, value ids/labels may now be reworded freely — an axis's rank numbers are the permanent part. Axis ids themselves are still referenced by entries as annotation keys and remain permanent.
Register model gpt-5-1 (GPT-5.1) — the visitor-prompt feature's OpenAI slot moves to the flagship pair (Claude Opus 5 vs GPT-5.1, jd-config.php).

Retire the "style" axis (owner call): defunct: true, the v6 mechanism — the survey stops asking it, jd-rate stops accepting it, the legend and report card drop it, and every filed style grading stays in the data untouched.

Relabel the three problem-shaped axes to one uniform scale (owner call): instruction-following, restraint and integrity now grade No problems / Small problems / Big problems (ranks unchanged — the v9 numeric filing makes this a pure rewording; per-axis descriptions keep the definitions). Je ne sais quoi keeps its labels pending its own rework — it grades a virtue, not a defect, and the problems framing does not fit it.

Relabel je ne sais quoi (owner call, completing the v12 pass): Has it / Just a hint / Ain't got it — the axis grades a virtue, so it gets a presence scale in plain speech rather than the defect axes' problems scale. Ranks unchanged; the filed descriptions keep the definitions.

Labels gain an _underscored emphasis_ convention (owner: italicize the it in "Has it"). HTML surfaces render the run in italics; plain-text surfaces (native option text, aria strings, stamped marks) strip the markers — JD_labelText in junk-drawer.js. Applied to je-ne-sais-quoi rank 3: Has _it_.
Spell out "Structural integrity" (owner call) — the integrity axis's display label, everywhere labels render (survey, popovers, legend, report card). The axis id stays integrity, as ids must.

Retire the "restraint" axis (owner call — possibly temporary): defunct: true, the v6 mechanism. The survey stops asking it, jd-rate stops accepting it, the report card and legend drop it; every filed restraint grading stays in the data, and un-retiring is one flag removal away.

The v17 rework (owner call, 2026-08-16): the placeholder rubric gives way to a benchmark-shaped one, and EVERY response starts blank under it — all five new axes get fresh ids, so nothing filed under the old rubric carries forward and a full re-rating pass follows. Retired (the v6 mechanism — filed gradings stay in the data, the survey and report card stop asking): instruction-following (superseded by understanding-assignment), integrity (its territory split between structural-coherence and layering) and je-ne-sais-quoi (superseded by jnsq — same scale and labels, new id purely so the slate is clean). The five new axes, in survey order: understanding-assignment "Understanding the Assignment" (4-point: Read the brief / Skimmed it / Misread it / Wrote its own brief) — comprehension of the brief, judged on what the model TRIED to draw; restraint-2 "Restraint" (the problems scale, re-scoped from the v16-retired restraint: gap-filling is the job, only upstaging additions are charged); layering "Layering" (4-point: Neat stack / A little shuffled / Out of order / Fifty-two pickup) — errors of the PICTURE: stacking, paint, framing — anything fixable without moving a path; structural-coherence "Structural Coherence" (the problems scale) — errors of the OBJECT: anything whose fix means redrawing geometry; jnsq "Je ne sais quoi" (Has _it_ / Just a hint / Ain't got it, unchanged). The picture/object bright line is written into the two axis descriptions so a defect has exactly one home. First 4-point scales in the taxonomy: their values file as ranks 4.0 … 1.0, the same v9 numeric convention.

Owner call, 2026-08-19, before any v17 rating was filed — so nothing is stranded and no re-rating is lost. Retired (v6 mechanism): restraint-2 "Restraint", folded into understanding-assignment. Living with the rubric showed the two asking one question: an unrequested addition that upstages the ask IS a failure to understand the assignment, and splitting it invited double-charging the same defect. understanding-assignment's description and its top three value descriptions now carry the negative-space test explicitly. layering drops from 4-point to the 3-point problems scale (No problems / Small problems / Big problems), matching structural-coherence: the picture and object axes are the same question about different territory, and asking them in different shapes made the survey harder to answer than the judgment warranted. Its old "Out of order" and "Fifty-two pickup" fold into Big problems. The rubric is now four axes: understanding-assignment (4-point), layering, structural-coherence and jnsq (3-point) — 308 cells across the 77 live responses, down from 385.

Owner call: structural-coherence moves to second, directly after understanding-assignment, ahead of layering. Survey order is display order everywhere — the turn survey, the record card, the how-to-read legend and the rating bench all iterate this array and filter defunct — so this one move reorders every instrument. The reading it produces: did the model understand the brief, is the OBJECT sound, is the PICTURE of it sound, and does it have _it_ — object before picture, since a well-drawn impossible thing is the more basic failure. Order only; no scale, id, label or description changed, and nothing already filed is affected (annotations key by axis id, ratings store axis_id).

Owner call: understanding-assignment's four value labels reworded from the brief metaphor (Read the brief / Skimmed it / Misread it / Wrote its own brief) to a plain comprehension scale — Fully Understands / Mostly Understands / Somewhat Understands / Barely Understands. Labels only; ranks, value ids, and descriptions are unchanged, so nothing already filed is affected (grades and ratings store rank numbers) and no code changes are needed — every instrument renders labels from this file.

Owner call: understanding-assignment's LABEL shortened from 'Understanding the Assignment' to 'Understanding Assignment' — the full phrase truncated in the bench's desktop subject column. Label only; the axis id, ranks, values and description are unchanged, so nothing filed is affected and no code changes are needed.

Owner call: understanding-assignment's DESCRIPTION reworded to plain rater-facing questions — intent, attempted subject matter, and overall resemblance to the prompt, execution issues set aside. Description only; the axis id, ranks and value labels/descriptions are unchanged, so nothing filed is affected.
